messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate in us-east-1 (20% errors, spike started at 2026-03-17T14:02:00Z). Auto-scaling attempts failing.

maria.chen: ack I'm on it, paging oncall.

jon.r: looking at model-runner-1 logs now — seeing repeated OOMs then segfaults on hot paths. grabbing the latest stacktrace.

jon.r: log snippet:
```
[14:02:15] runner: Alloc failed: attempted 2.1GB, avail 1.9GB
[14:02:15] runner: eviction triggered for kvcache shard 3
[14:02:16] runner: SIGSEGV at 0x7f12a3c4
[14:02:16] core dumped -> /var/crash/runner-1.core
```

sara_k: confirmed similar from runner-3, pattern looks like abrupt mmap/alloc growth during long-context requests. Customer traffic bump?

ops-bot: traffic-manager reports a slow ramp of large-context requests (avg seq len 2.8x normal) from a handful of API keys.

maria.chen: mitigation plan: 1) reduce concurrency per-runner to 1 for affected pool 2) enable routing to model-variant fallback (smaller context / quantized) 3) collect cores and attach debugger if crash reproduces. I'll apply 1 & 2 now.

jon.r: ran: `kubectl -n inference set env deployment/runner-pool CONCURRENCY=1 --record` -> rolling update started. Also pushed traffic rule: route 30% -> model-v1-small via traffic-manager.

maria.chen: monitoring... error rate dropped to 12% after routing change. still seeing occasional SIGSEGVs on a few pods.

leo: @maria.chen I'm taking the pager, will dig deeper. Can we get a core from one of the crashed pods?

jon.r: core available: `/var/crash/runner-1.core` on node ip 10.2.14.8. I copied it to /tmp and uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/6324001111/core-runner-1.core.

leo: grabbing it. plan: run `gdb --batch --quiet --ex "thread apply all bt full" -c core /opt/runner/bin/runner > bt.txt` and see top frames. If it's allocator or jemalloc we can hotpatch disable large-alloc fastpaths.

cs_lead: any customer impact? Which tenants affected?

ops-bot: impact list: keys A12*, B34* (2 high-traffic customers), estimated 18% of requests in us-east-1. No data loss, only latency/errors.

maria.chen: notifying CS and sending ETA for mitigation window. Started gradual traffic reroute to other regions as fallback for impacted API keys.

leo: GDB output points to crash inside attention kernel during large-ctx matmul (frame: attention::compute_kv +0x4f). Suspect kernel memory indexing bug under high-seqlen.

jon.r: we can temporarily block requests with seq_len > 2048 via gateway rule to reduce risk. Deploying that now.

maria.chen: blocking >2048 in gateway applied. error rate fell to ~3% and latency back to normal for routed traffic. Keeping rollback plans in case.

leo: opened an internal issue with repro steps and assigned to eng-runtime (link: https://github.com/redwood/infer-runtime/issues/9876). Suggest immediate hotpatch to attention kernel to add bounds check; I'm preparing a minimal patch.

maria.chen: for now: mitigation status = partial (traffic rerouted + seq_len block). Next steps: hotpatch + canary, full patch in next deploy. I'll keep paging if regression observed.

jon.r: thumbs up. capturing post-incident notes and core dumps stored.\\n
cs_lead: emailed affected customers with summary and mitigation steps. will follow up with timeline for permanent fix.

maria.chen: handing off to leo for deeper debug and patching. leo oncall until 15:30 UTC. If anything spikes, please @pagerduty. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
